description: Advisory security-sink catalogue. Each entry is a declarative rule over a payload FIELD (field x operator x pattern, AND-combined) that the guardrail runtime may evaluate to surface a risk. It is DATA, not policy: a match produces an advisory, never a deny. Rule ids are FROZEN — append new entries with a new id, never renumber. Every reminder carries the MITIGATION, not just the alert.

patterns.reminder: Untrusted pickle deserialization executes arbitrary code. Prefer a data-only format (JSON, MessagePack); if pickle is unavoidable, load only from a trusted, integrity-checked source.
os.system runs the argument through a shell. Prefer an argument-vector call (subprocess with a list) so untrusted input cannot inject a command.
shell=True hands the string to a shell. Pass an argument list and drop shell=True unless the command is a fixed, non-interpolated string.
Disabling certificate verification permits a man-in-the-middle. Fix the trust store or pin the certificate instead of turning verification off.
ECB leaks structure: equal plaintext blocks produce equal ciphertext blocks. Use an authenticated mode (GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305).
yaml.load without a safe loader can construct arbitrary objects. Use yaml.safe_load, or pass SafeLoader explicitly. Multi-line calls may not match — this is a known limitation.
Piping a download straight into a shell executes unverified remote code. Download, verify a checksum or signature, then run the local file.
Interpolating attacker-controlled GitHub context into a run step is script injection. Pass the value through an env var and quote it, or use a safer action.
MD5 and SHA-1 are not password hashes: they are fast and unsalted. Use a memory-hard scheme (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2) for passwords.
Exempting a view from CSRF protection removes a defense against forged requests. Confirm the endpoint is token-authenticated and not state-changing, and add an inline justification comment.
